title: LONGEVITY SURVIVOR v2.1 — Lock-Aligned Cross-Tissue Overlay
frozen_question: When HEART, COCHLEA, SPINAL_CORD, SKIN and TENDON are aligned by the relative moment when high-fidelity regeneration is lost rather than by chronological age, which state transitions recur across tissues?

alignment_rule.BEFORE_LOCK: tau < 0; tissue still shows high-fidelity or substantially more complete regeneration
alignment_rule.LOCK_TRANSITION: tau ~= 0; developmental interval in which regenerative competence sharply declines or scar-biased repair becomes dominant
alignment_rule.AFTER_LOCK: tau > 0; regeneration is strongly limited, incomplete, lineage-restricted, or replaced by fibrosis/scarring
alignment_rule.important: tau=0 is tissue-specific and is not assumed to correspond to the same postnatal day, gestational week, species age, or pathway amplitude.

tissue_overlays.model: mammalian neonatal heart, strongest mechanistic data in mouse
tissue_overlays.lock_anchor: brief neonatal regenerative window; exact timing is model-dependent, with strong mouse evidence for rapid postnatal loss

BEFORE_LOCK.plasticity: pre-existing cardiomyocytes retain substantially greater proliferative/dedifferentiation competence; epicardial developmental programs remain more active
BEFORE_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: cardiac ECM is softer and compositionally more development-like
BEFORE_LOCK.immune: resident/embryonic-derived macrophage programs are enriched and support angiogenesis/reparative signaling
BEFORE_LOCK.cell_cycle: cardiomyocyte mitotic competence is substantially higher
BEFORE_LOCK.fibrosis: injury-associated matrix/scar can be transient and resolve during successful regeneration
BEFORE_LOCK.exit: successful regeneration terminates after structure/function recovery rather than remaining constitutively proliferative

LOCK_TRANSITION.plasticity: cardiomyocyte and epicardial developmental competence declines
LOCK_TRANSITION.ecm_mechanics: rapid ECM stiffening/crosslinking and compositional maturation occurs near the loss window; experimental softening plus fetal ECM can extend regenerative behavior in low-regenerative neonatal hearts
LOCK_TRANSITION.immune: resident regenerative macrophage balance shifts toward more monocyte-derived/pro-inflammatory adult-like responses
LOCK_TRANSITION.cell_cycle: cell-cycle competence falls with cardiomyocyte maturation, although some studies indicate ECM changes can precede full cell-cycle arrest
LOCK_TRANSITION.fibrosis: scar resolution becomes less efficient and permanent collagenous repair becomes favored
LOCK_TRANSITION.exit: adult-like repair terminates by stabilization/remodeling rather than restoration of lost myocardium

AFTER_LOCK.plasticity: mature cardiomyocytes are strongly cell-cycle restricted
AFTER_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: stiffer mature matrix constrains pro-regenerative signaling
AFTER_LOCK.cell_cycle: replacement of lost myocardium by cardiomyocyte proliferation is insufficient
AFTER_LOCK.fibrosis: permanent fibrotic scar is the dominant outcome after major injury
AFTER_LOCK.exit: repair exits into stable scar/homeostasis, not anatomical regeneration

evidence: JACC Focus Seminar: rapid mouse ventricular stiffness increase near earliest postnatal loss window; lowering ECM stiffness prolongs regeneration
PMCID:PMC7428869 — fetal ECM + softening increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity and lowers fibrosis
Nature Reviews Cardiology 2024 — neonatal vs adult mammalian cardiac regeneration
eLife 2025 DOI:10.7554/eLife.107419 — extending embryonic-like epicardial HIF activity improves regeneration beyond the usual window
Frontiers Cell Dev Biol 2024 — developmental macrophage composition differs across regenerative vs non-regenerative heart states

tissue_overlays.lock_anchor: regenerative competence falls rapidly after birth and is largely lost before/around hearing maturation

BEFORE_LOCK.plasticity: supporting/prosensory cells retain progenitor-like competence and can generate hair-cell-like descendants more readily
BEFORE_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: developing cochlear niche is not yet fully mechanically and architecturally mature
BEFORE_LOCK.immune: not established as the dominant developmental lock axis
BEFORE_LOCK.fibrosis: fibrosis is not the primary lock phenotype; failure is more lineage/epigenetic than classic scar formation
BEFORE_LOCK.exit: development normally terminates regenerative/developmental competence as sensory architecture matures

LOCK_TRANSITION.plasticity: enhancer decommissioning, H3K4me1 loss, DNA methylation and reduced accessibility stabilize supporting-cell identity and reduce hair-cell fate competence
LOCK_TRANSITION.ecm_mechanics: architectural maturation occurs but current evidence does not support matrix stiffness as the primary universal cochlear lock
LOCK_TRANSITION.immune: immune niche can shape repair after injury, but developmental synchronization with regeneration loss is not yet strong enough for P0
LOCK_TRANSITION.cell_cycle: supporting cells become increasingly refractory to proliferation and reprogramming
LOCK_TRANSITION.fibrosis: not a canonical scar transition; mark as tissue-specific exception
LOCK_TRANSITION.exit: maturation effectively closes a developmental permission state rather than merely ending an acute wound program

AFTER_LOCK.plasticity: mature supporting cells retain some residual substrate but are strongly epigenetically locked
AFTER_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: mature organ architecture imposes additional integration constraints
AFTER_LOCK.immune: repair-associated macrophages can aid synaptic repair but do not restore full hair-cell regenerative competence
AFTER_LOCK.exit: mature stable sensory architecture is preserved at the cost of regenerative flexibility

evidence: eLife 2019 DOI:10.7554/eLife.44328 — mature cochlear supporting cells show lower hair-cell-locus accessibility than regenerative utricle supporting cells
PNAS 2023 — DNA methylation promotes supporting-cell maturation and contributes to regenerative failure
Developmental Cell 2021 — enhancer decommissioning imposes epigenetic barrier
PNAS 2024 — long-range Atoh1 enhancers maintain regenerative competency
World Journal of Stem Cells 2026 review — postnatal competence loss summarized as enhancer decommissioning/H3K4me1 loss/DNA methylation

tissue_overlays.model: neonatal vs later mouse spinal-cord injury response
tissue_overlays.lock_anchor: age-dependent decline in scar-free healing and long-tract axon regrowth

BEFORE_LOCK.plasticity: axon regrowth and neonatal repair programs are substantially more permissive
BEFORE_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: injury generates a temporary fibronectin-rich bridge rather than an immediately persistent mature fibroglial scar
BEFORE_LOCK.immune: neonatal microglia are transiently activated and express programs associated with inflammation resolution
BEFORE_LOCK.cell_cycle: support-cell/glial response is organized toward bridging and resolution rather than persistent scar containment
BEFORE_LOCK.fibrosis: scar-free or markedly reduced scar healing can occur
BEFORE_LOCK.exit: microglial activation and temporary ECM bridge resolve after reconnection

LOCK_TRANSITION.ecm_mechanics: temporary regenerative bridge is replaced by a lesion environment dominated by mature fibroblast/astroglial scar architecture
LOCK_TRANSITION.immune: microglial/macrophage response loses neonatal pro-resolving configuration
LOCK_TRANSITION.cell_cycle: supportive injury-response cell states no longer recreate the neonatal bridge effectively
LOCK_TRANSITION.exit: wound response exits into stable scar containment rather than bridge-resolution-restoration

AFTER_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: scar ECM and inhibitory matrix dominate lesion organization
AFTER_LOCK.immune: adult inflammatory/glial states persist differently from neonatal microglia
AFTER_LOCK.cell_cycle: cellular response stabilizes the lesion but does not recreate the original neural architecture
AFTER_LOCK.exit: repair reaches containment rather than full reconnection

evidence: Nature 2020 DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2795-6 — neonatal microglia form transient fibronectin bridge, resolve inflammation, enable scar-free healing; adult/neonatal transplantation experiments support causality
Neuroscience Bulletin 2022 — spatiotemporal adult glial scar comparison

tissue_overlays.model: fetal scarless mammalian skin vs postnatal/adult scarring skin; adult mechanotransduction models
tissue_overlays.lock_anchor: developmental transition from fetal scarless regeneration to postnatal scar-forming repair; exact gestational timing is species-specific

BEFORE_LOCK.plasticity: fetal fibroblasts and epidermal programs support restoration with appendage/ECM architecture more faithfully
BEFORE_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: HA-rich, less crosslinked, development-like matrix with rapid turnover
BEFORE_LOCK.immune: brief/minimal inflammatory response with rapid resolution
BEFORE_LOCK.cell_cycle: fetal cells retain high proliferative/migratory competence
BEFORE_LOCK.fibrosis: myofibroblast presence is absent, reduced or transient; collagen organization returns toward normal
BEFORE_LOCK.exit: wound program terminates after restoration rather than persistent myofibroblast activity

LOCK_TRANSITION.plasticity: fibroblast fate becomes more mechanically coupled to profibrotic states
LOCK_TRANSITION.ecm_mechanics: increased tissue tension/mechanotransduction favors YAP/TAZ-dependent scar-forming fibroblast trajectories
LOCK_TRANSITION.immune: postnatal wounds develop stronger and more sustained inflammatory signaling
LOCK_TRANSITION.cell_cycle: proliferation remains available but is increasingly routed into repair/fibrosis rather than architecture restoration
LOCK_TRANSITION.exit: scar-producing states are not cleared as rapidly as fetal wound states

AFTER_LOCK.plasticity: adult fibroblasts remain plastic enough to scar and can be experimentally rerouted, showing the machinery is not simply absent
AFTER_LOCK.immune: inflammation and mechanics interact to reinforce repair trajectories
AFTER_LOCK.cell_cycle: cell proliferation closes wounds but does not reliably regenerate appendages/normal architecture
AFTER_LOCK.fibrosis: scar is the dominant mammalian outcome

evidence: fetal wound literature — low/promptly resolved inflammation, HA-rich ECM, transient myofibroblast states and scarless outcome
Mascharak et al lineage/mechanotransduction work — mechanical tension/YAP can convert regenerative fibroblast potential toward scar-forming fate in mouse skin
Science Translational Medicine 2025 large-animal work summarized by Stanford profile — local YAP/mechanotransduction inhibition drove more regenerative porcine wound healing
Burns & Trauma 2026 spatiotemporal skin review — YAP/TAZ/TEAD accessibility and mechanics linked to fibrotic fibroblast trajectories

tissue_overlays.model: neonatal vs adult mouse Achilles tendon healing
tissue_overlays.lock_anchor: neonatal regenerative competence is present before approximately postnatal day 7 in mouse models and is absent in adult tendon

BEFORE_LOCK.plasticity: resident Scx-lineage tenocytes proliferate and are recruited into the defect
BEFORE_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: developing tendon niche supports organized neo-tendon formation
BEFORE_LOCK.immune: not yet established as the sole master lock; niche/lymphatic signaling contributes
BEFORE_LOCK.cell_cycle: injured neonatal tenocytes show strong proliferation and recruitment
BEFORE_LOCK.fibrosis: extrinsic alpha-SMA-positive cells are recruited transiently but do not persist as permanent scar
BEFORE_LOCK.exit: transient wound cells leave/resolve as intrinsic tenocytes rebuild aligned tendon

LOCK_TRANSITION.plasticity: stemness/progenitor-associated tendon states decline during maturation
LOCK_TRANSITION.ecm_mechanics: tendon niche matures toward dense low-cellularity ECM and altered stem-cell support
LOCK_TRANSITION.immune: lymphatic niche signaling and macrophage state influence regenerative outcome; developmental synchronization requires more direct time-series evidence
LOCK_TRANSITION.cell_cycle: resident tenocyte recruitment/proliferation competence is lost
LOCK_TRANSITION.fibrosis: extrinsic alpha-SMA-positive repair cells shift from transient helpers to persistent scar contributors
LOCK_TRANSITION.exit: wound-state resolution fails to restore tenogenic occupancy of the defect

AFTER_LOCK.plasticity: adult tenocytes can reactivate some tendon programs but are not properly recruited into the defect and may undergo aberrant differentiation
AFTER_LOCK.ecm_mechanics: fibrovascular scar and disorganized matrix dominate repair
AFTER_LOCK.immune: adult repair remains inflammatory/fibrotic with altered niche support
AFTER_LOCK.cell_cycle: adult Scx-lineage tenocytes remain largely quiescent after transection
AFTER_LOCK.exit: repair terminates in mechanically inferior scar rather than neo-tendon

evidence: Scientific Reports 2017 DOI:10.1038/srep45238 — neonatal Scx-lineage proliferation/recruitment and transient alpha-SMA cells vs adult persistent scar
eLife 2020 DOI:10.7554/eLife.51779 — TGF-beta is required for neonatal tenocyte recruitment, showing pathway context rather than scalar anti-fibrosis logic

Nature Communications 2026 (published 26 Dec 2025) — neonatal-before-P7 vs adult tendon single-cell comparison identifies lymphatic vessels as regenerative niche elements; stemness scores decline from tendon stem cells to mature tenocytes; Reelin loss impairs regeneration

P0_A.name: RESIDENT_REGENERATIVE_COMPETENCE_COLLAPSE
P0_A.relative_alignment: clusters around tau ~= 0 by construction because each tissue loses regenerative competence as the relevant resident cells become less proliferative, less recruitable or more lineage-locked
P0_A.why_P0: This is the cleanest repeated intrinsic transition across at least three unrelated tissues and is supported by functional perturbation or lineage/epigenetic evidence.
P0_A.claim_ceiling: A common functional transition is supported; no single molecular switch is established.

P0_B.name: TRANSIENT_WOUND_STATE_TO_PERSISTENT_SCAR_STATE
P0_B.exception: COCHLEA does not use classic fibrosis as the dominant lock phenotype and therefore should not be forced into this module.
P0_B.relative_alignment: the regenerative side uses temporary injury states that are actively resolved; the non-regenerative side stabilizes those states or their descendants as scar/containment
P0_B.why_P0: Three tissues independently show the same topology: transient bridge/helper/myofibroblast-like state is compatible with regeneration; persistence predicts scar-biased repair.
P0_B.claim_ceiling: The shared invariant is persistence-versus-resolution, not identity of one cell type or cytokine.

P0_C.name: NICHE_MECHANICAL_MATURATION
P0_C.relative_alignment: mechanical/matrix maturation is near tau=0 in heart and developmentally coupled to postnatal scarring in skin; in spinal cord/tendon the strongest evidence is a switch in injury-matrix architecture rather than a directly measured universal stiffness threshold
P0_C.why_not_P0_full: Current evidence supports a strong cross-tissue candidate but not yet a clean 3-tissue causal developmental stiffness transition.

P1_IMMUNE.name: REGENERATIVE_IMMUNE_RESOLUTION_SHIFT
P1_IMMUNE.reason: Immune timing and cell identities differ substantially by tissue; evidence does not yet justify one synchronized universal immune lock.

P1_CHROMATIN.name: EPIGENETIC_PERMISSION_CLOSURE
P1_CHROMATIN.reason: Cochlea has unusually direct enhancer/methylation evidence, but equivalent tau-aligned chromatin time series are not yet recovered for all five tissues.

topa_falsification.claim: All six axes close synchronously in all five tissues.
topa_falsification.reason: Cochlea is dominated by epigenetic/lineage locking rather than classical fibrosis, and several tissues lack matched measurements on all axes.

topa_falsification.claim: YAP is the universal regeneration ON switch.
topa_falsification.reason: YAP can support regeneration in some contexts but promote fibrosis in others; interpretation depends on cell type, mechanics, timing, partners and duration.

topa_falsification.claim: TGF-beta inhibition is a universal anti-fibrotic route to regeneration.
topa_falsification.reason: TGF-beta is required for neonatal tenocyte recruitment and adult zebrafish tendon regeneration despite pro-fibrotic roles in other contexts.

topa_falsification.claim: Regeneration loss is caused only by cell-cycle arrest.
topa_falsification.reason: Heart ECM changes can precede full cardiomyocyte cell-cycle loss; spinal cord and skin demonstrate niche/immune/scar-routing contributions; cochlea demonstrates epigenetic competence loss.

topa_falsification.claim: The common gate is one conserved gene.
topa_falsification.reason: The strongest recurrence is topological and state-based: permission, transient wound state, niche, resolution and exit.

survivor_v2_1.name: REVERSIBLE_MATURATION_LOCK_WITH_RESOLUTION
survivor_v2_1.formula: LOCAL_ENTRY_PERMISSION + RESIDENT_CELL_COMPETENCE + PERMISSIVE_NICHE + TEMPORARY_WOUND_STATE + PATTERNED_REBUILD + RESOLUTION + MANDATORY_EXIT
survivor_v2_1.interpretation: The mammalian regeneration lock currently looks more like a coordinated state transition than a missing pathway. Successful regeneration repeatedly requires both entry into a temporary plastic state and reliable resolution back to stable tissue identity.

next_killer_tests.test: Recover matched before/transition/after single-cell or multi-omic datasets for all five tissues and project them into the same six-axis state space without using gene-name overlap as the alignment criterion.
next_killer_tests.pass_condition: At least three tissues show the same directional transition on an axis with independent causal or perturbational support.

next_killer_tests.test: Quantify persistence half-life of wound-state cells/matrix across regenerative and non-regenerative conditions: neonatal microglia bridge, fetal/adult myofibroblasts, neonatal/adult tendon alpha-SMA cells, neonatal/adult cardiac scar fibroblasts.
next_killer_tests.pass_condition: Regenerative conditions consistently show shorter-lived helper/scar states followed by lineage-correct replacement.

next_killer_tests.test: Find a third tissue with direct causal evidence that developmental ECM/mechanical maturation at tau~=0 suppresses regenerative competence and that reversing the mechanical state restores it without merely delaying wound closure.
next_killer_tests.pass_condition: NICHE_MECHANICAL_MATURATION promotes from P0 candidate to hard survivor.

next_killer_tests.test: Separate ENTRY machinery from EXIT machinery in each tissue and test whether regenerative failure is caused by failure to enter, failure to rebuild, failure to resolve, or failure to exit.
next_killer_tests.pass_condition: At least three tissues share the same failure topology even if molecular implementations differ.

boundary: Comparative developmental biology and hypothesis ranking only. This artifact does not provide a human treatment, dosing plan, gene-editing protocol, rejuvenation procedure, or evidence that manipulating these gates is safe in humans.
